sections.h2: What an SLA becomes once it is in software
paras: A service level agreement is a promise with a number in it: attend within so many hours, restore within so many more. SLA management software turns that promise into something the service desk can see. Each contract carries its own response and resolution targets, every call logged against a covered asset starts a clock, and calls approaching their limit are visible before they breach rather than after.

Aura Business holds this as SLA Definitions and Breach Tracking in the AMC and Service Contracts suite, with SLA timers also running on helpdesk tickets. It is one of the few modules whose value is entirely about timing. A breach found the next morning is a report. A call flagged at hour three is a save.

sections.h2: Most breaches are not capacity problems. They are visibility problems.
sections.lead: Nobody decides to miss a response time. The call simply sits in a queue where nothing indicates it is different from the others.

items.p: A four-hour contract and a next-day contract sit in the same list looking identical.

items.h: The clock exists only in the contract
items.p: The response time is in a PDF nobody on the service desk has read.
The first anyone hears of it is an angry call from the hospital's biomedical head.

items.q: Can different customers have different SLAs?
items.a: Yes, and that is the point of holding them on the contract. A four-hour response for a teaching hospital and a next-working-day response for a small clinic both apply automatically to calls raised against their own assets.

items.q: When does the response clock start and stop?
items.a: It starts when the call is logged and stops when the engineer is recorded as attending, which in practice is the GPS check-in on the mobile app. The resolution clock runs until the job is closed.

items.q: What happens when a call is about to breach?
items.a: It is flagged on the service desk and escalated to the owner you have nominated, so a decision can be made to reassign, send a second engineer or inform the customer before the window closes.

items.q: Do helpdesk tickets have SLAs too?
items.a: Yes. SLA timers run on tickets in the Ticketing and Helpdesk suite as well as on field service calls. See helpdesk ticketing.

items.q: Does missing an SLA calculate a penalty automatically?
items.a: The breach is recorded with its times. Whether a penalty applies, and how it is computed, depends on your contract wording, so the platform gives you the evidence rather than a commercial judgement.

items.q: How does this help at renewal?
items.a: The contract carries its call history, response times and resolutions, so the renewal is discussed against the record. See contract management and AMC billing.
